correctness.rationale: The nontrivial occupancy cylinders are {000,100}, {010,011}, and {101,111}; the other two rows select all cells. Agreement on a selected prefix preserves the occupancy bit and endpoint there, so the table gives a graph-measurable stopping set on all locally finite counting measures. Measurability follows by measurable cell counts and first-point thresholds. For the diffuse PPP each occupied prefix contributes exactly one point almost surely and the row counts are 0,1,1,1,0,2,2,2. On the empty configuration (an atom of probability exp(-3)) the final target has measure 2, hence monotone intensity-continuity gives a finite deterministic t before attainment with U=A_t(0) of measure in (0,1). This also holds if attainment at infinity is allowed as the increasing union. U meets C2 or C3 in positive measure. On a positive-probability no-hit-in-U event the occupancy is 101 if C2 was met or 010 if C3 was met: prescribe the points in the necessary cell complements, each of positive measure. The stopping-set property fixes the observed history through t, so attainment is still ahead and the omitted part of U cannot be removed. Even for a completed observed-history filtration, the event of agreeing histories through t is an observation atom containing the empty configuration, which cannot be changed by a null exception. The same contradiction can avoid the stopping-time property altogether: choose measure(U)<1/4 and require all prescribed points in the final quarters of their cells outside U, making target mass >1, so attainment before t is impossible by mass monotonicity. This is a continuum proof; check_result.py was inspected but not executed, and its finite cases cannot establish nonattainment.

evidence: In LPY Example 2 substitute X_1=1-b_1, X_2=1-b_2, X_3=b_3. Its three pair-output conditions become precisely the reviewed table, with full-cell selection on 001 and 110. This is an equivalence of the index rule, not of the stopping sets, because LPY reveals complete selected cells, with unbounded counts. Prefix truncation of the unmodified LPY rule alone would still reveal three on 111.

Bit complementation is not a spatial relabeling of the actual Poisson configurations.

originality.rationale: Pass for the at-most-two diffuse threshold example and nonattainment under modulo-intensity stopping, not for the underlying three-cell decision logic or the general existence of nonattainable stopping sets. The closest whole-cell example has precisely the same Boolean rule after complementing two input bits, important structural overlap. The complement and first-point truncation together are needed to retain the obstruction under the stringent actual revealed-point budget. Neither the inspected whole-cell theorem nor the one-point attainability theorem contains the resulting bounded-point counterexample.
residual_risks: The search was bounded to plausible catalogue matches and the main cited texts; an unindexed equivalent bounded-count construction remains possible.
No originality is assigned to the Boolean table itself, and no claim is made about minimal cell count, other intensity regimes or arbitrary discontinuous algorithms.

value.rationale: A sharp threshold at two revealed points answers the immediate next case of the one-point theorem. Achieving it with a graph-measurable set on a compact diffuse model, and defeating even intensity-equivalent explored regions, are substantive constraints; the earlier examples with unbounded revealed counts could not answer this threshold question.
